name: Drug shortages and compounding
scope: FDA-approved drug products determined to be in shortage
direct_answer: When FDA determines a drug is in national shortage, certain compounding restrictions are relaxed. When the shortage resolves, those exceptions end after any announced transition period.

definitions.definition: A period when demand or projected demand within the U.S. exceeds supply, determined on a nationwide basis.
FDA's decision not to take action for a defined period, not a change in the law.

decision_logic: 1. Is the approved drug on FDA's drug shortage list? 2. If yes, compounding copies may be allowed under 503A/503B for the duration. 3. When FDA declares the shortage resolved, copy restrictions return; FDA may provide a transition period. 4. Local stock-outs do not equal a national shortage.
examples: Tirzepatide injection was on the shortage list; after FDA resolved the shortage on 2024-12-19, 503A copies became restricted again.
limitations: A shortage determination does not approve a new drug.
FDA's list is national, not local.
